result.title: From Small to Large: Assessing Medical Reasoning, Benchmark Contamination, and Model Size in Language Models
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) now answer medical exam questions at or above expert level, but it is unclear whether such scores reflect clinical competence, or are instead affected by the format of the questions being asked (e.g., multiple-choice versus open-ended), prior exposure to the benchmarks, and the difficulty of the questions. These benchmarks are also public and widely used online, which may be resulting in LLM memorization. Models may perform better on questions that they have seen before. It is also not evident whether smaller models, which are more locally deployable in HIPAA-compliant hospital settings, have achieved human performance. In this study, we evaluate fourteen current models from six leading providers, one smaller and one larger model from each provider with two additional open-weight models, on 3,076 questions from four medical benchmarks (MedQA-USMLE, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, and MedBullets) under standard multiple choice, the same questions with the answer choices withheld, and reconstruction of a hidden question from its choices alone. In the standard multiple-choice setting, the strongest models exceed the human-expert baseline on MedQA-USMLE and PubMedQA, but the smaller models trail their larger models by 8.7 percentage points and only two of the six pass the human-expert bar on the licensing examination. Withholding the answer choices, however, makes every model struggle: mean accuracy falls from 82.3% to 50.9%, and the two largest drops belong to the medically specialised models. On memorization, the strongest models reconstruct one question in four from the answer choices alone, yet accuracy holds on the questions they cannot reconstruct. We further weigh accuracy against inference cost and test whether ensembling several models improves medical question answering.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在四个医学基准共 3076 题上评测来自六家厂商的 14 个模型，比较标准多选题、隐去选项、以及仅凭选项重建题目三种设置，考察模型规模、基准污染与推理成本对医学答题表现的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 隐去选项后平均准确率从 82.3% 降至 50.9% 的现象，可能为 LVR 中「答案是否真正依赖必要证据、抑或被格式线索短路」的评价设计提供参照，其与视觉旁路的可类比性可供核查。
